mode: MEASUREMENT AND CENSUS. No optimization performed. Every loading-order change is a DECISION_REQUIRED candidate in DECISION_BOARD.md.

instruments.route_census: assets/tests/_s4r1-route-census-runner.js - every user-visible route entered cold, left, and re-entered warm, in one real headless Chrome, over S3-R11's fixture world (imported, not copied).
instruments.shell_timing: assets/tests/_s4r1-shell-timing-runner.js - the Chrome PROCESS timed from Node, because the page has no honest clock under virtual time.

what_is_authoritative: Request counts and the actions behind them. A count is a property of control flow, and the two serverMs settings demonstrate that rather than asserting it.
READ ROUNDS, but ONLY from the 400 ms run - see the caveat below.
DOM outcomes: shell-before-data, useful content, skeletons, visible-section count, open requests on leave.
Listener and interval drift, counted at addEventListener/removeEventListener and setInterval/clearInterval, wrapped before any application script runs.
The boot payload, read from disk against index.html.
what_is_not_observable: MILLISECONDS OF CLIENT WORK. Measured, not assumed: under --virtual-time-budget Chrome freezes the clock while a task executes, so a page running `while (Date.now() - t < 300) {}` NEVER TERMINATES. performance.now() deltas count poll ticks.

Timing the Chrome process from outside does not rescue it at this scale: single-entry route deltas (-82 to +154 ms) sit INSIDE the baseline run's own spread (840 ms), and two of them are NEGATIVE - a route cannot cost less than doing nothing, which is what a measurement drowned in noise looks like. The 20-cycle amplification loops did not complete their cycles, so their per-entry figures are refused by name rather than published with a caveat.
SHELL vs PARTIAL vs JS vs RENDER cannot be separated from outside the process.
instrument_caveats: ROUND COUNTS AT serverMs 0 ARE WRONG, AND THE 400 ms RUN IS WHY THEY ARE IN HERE TWICE. With instant settles, request N+1 is always SENT after request N SETTLED, so a pooled read looks perfectly sequential. campaign-risk reads 5/5 rounds at 0 ms and 5/3 at 400 ms; ceil(5/2) = 3 is the read pool (KM_SCOPED_READ_CONCURRENCY_ = 2) behaving exactly as designed. Every round count quoted in the report is the 400 ms one.
sku-handbook issues 3 requests at 0 ms and 2 at 400 ms. That is not noise: overlapping requests become eligible for the transport in-flight share, which cannot coalesce reads that never overlap.

Routes whose tables this fixture world does not carry render no rows. They are recorded with useful:0 and are NOT scored as "never becomes useful" - the census reports what each route ASKED FOR, which is fixture-independent.
The timeout counter in the shell block is contaminated by the instrument's own 8 ms polling and is not reported.

boot_payload.note: Every local script is loaded by index.html at boot. 79 of 82 carry `defer`, so they do not block HTML parsing - but defer still runs them all, in order, BEFORE DOMContentLoaded, which is when the menu becomes usable. Bytes are uncompressed on disk; the wire cost depends on server compression, but PARSE and EXECUTE cost is paid on these bytes regardless.

shell_timing.what_this_excludes: Server latency (serverMs=0). Shell / partial / JS / render cannot be separated from outside the process and are reported as NOT_OBSERVABLE.
shell_timing.verdict: NO stop point exceeds the baseline spread. Per-route CLIENT cost is below this instrument’s resolution (~840 ms), which is itself the finding: every route, including the heaviest, completes inside the same band as doing nothing at all. The seconds an operator waits in production are therefore not client render or script time.
